newsitem.title: GERMANY: Allianz - German non-life sales to fall.
newsitem.headline: Allianz - German non-life sales to fall.

text.p: Allianz Versicherungs AG, the domestic non-life unit of Allianz AG Holding, said on Tuesday it expected its premium income to show a further slight decline this year but said profits should be good.
In a speech prepared for a news conference, Allianz Versicherungs chairman Reiner Hegemann said he expected continued weakness in the insurance market this year.

The German insurance unit reported a 1.4 percent decline in 1996 premium income to 17.1 billion marks ($10.2 billion) but a 41.4 percent rise in pre-tax profit to 1.6 billion marks, which it attributed to unusually favourable claims and strong new business.

"For 1997 we are expecting continued weak growth in the market, caused by a stagnation, in the best case senario, in net income, a continued clearly weak economy and ongoing price pressures," Hagemann said.

"Overall we expect a continued slight fall in premium income in 1997. The measures so far introduced to manage costs and claims will be extended and will hopefully contribute to another good result," he added.
Hagemann also said that the integration of the non-life business of the Vereinte group, which Allianz took over in full last year, would be an important focus in 1997.
